flashcard_questions.q: What is a power chord made of?
flashcard_questions.a: Just the root note and the 5th.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is a power chord neither major nor minor?
flashcard_questions.a: It leaves out the 3rd, the note that decides major or minor.

flashcard_questions.q: Which notes make up a G5 power chord?
Why do power chords suit distortion better than full triads?
flashcard_questions.a: With only two notes they stay clear and punchy under distortion.
An effect that clips the signal to give a harsh, gritty tone.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a mild form of distortion called?

flashcard_questions.a: A studio technique placing a sound left, right or centre.

flashcard_questions.q: Which instrument is most commonly panned in recorded rock?
Why is panning not the same as volume?
flashcard_questions.a: It controls where a sound sits in the stereo field.
Singing higher than the singer's normal range.
A short repeated melodic or rhythmic pattern.

flashcard_questions.q: What separates a riff from a one-off melodic phrase?
flashcard_questions.a: The riff is repeated several times.

flashcard_questions.q: Which scale gives many rock riffs their bluesy feel?
Which instrument underpins the harmony and locks in with the drums?
What does the drum kit contribute to a rock track?
flashcard_questions.a: Driving rhythms that keep the momentum and intensity.

notes: 15 cards: 4 power-chord cards (construction, why it is neither major nor minor, the G5 example, why it suits distortion), 5 technology cards (distortion, overdrive, panning, what is panned, the panning-versus-volume misconception), 3 melody cards (riff, what makes it a riff, minor pentatonic), and 3 instrument-role cards including falsetto. The band line-up list was split into role cards so no answer is an enumeration.
